1. Untyped lambda calculus can be modeled with 1 iota axiom
  2. boolean logic - too 1 axiom (not axiom actually, but 1 algebraic identity, operating inside standard equational substitution rules, e.g. Birkhoff's Equational Logic)
  3. Propositional logic - 2 axioms (e.g. Meredith + Modus Ponens)
  4. Minimal known Universal Turing Computer - 2 states, 3 symbols (dont know how much axioms it needs)
  5. based on this **lean4** model in mm0 -

lean is using 271 axioms

  • 12 Utility Axioms: Basic list operations, conjunctions (mk_and), and boolean logic (or_nat).
  • 22 Universe Level Axioms: Rules for level substitutions and ordering (l_subst_var, l_pl_imax_imax_left, etc.).
  • 25 Expression & Substitution Axioms: Alpha equivalence, term substitutions (subst_app, subst_lambda, etc.).
  • 20 Type-Checking & Conversion Rules: Typing universe levels, application, lambda abstraction, beta/eta conversions (ty_app, conv_beta, conv_eta, proof_irrel).
  • 178 Inductive Type & Recursor Axioms: Rules for strict positivity, mutual inductive declarations, recursors, structures, and $i$-reduction (pos_M_0, ctor_app, ty_Rec, iota_reduction, conv_eta_proj).
  • 14 Non-Primitive Axioms: Quotient types (ty_quot_sound, quot_iota), Propositional Extensionality (ty_propext), and Classical Choice (ty_choice).

But

  1. What is the minimal amount of axioms one can compress Calculus of Constructions to? 1? 2?
  2. Lean axioms?
  3. Higher Observational Type Theory axioms? (today's best, right?)

This compression of axioms will advance math, right?

P.S. also posted on cstheory.stackexchange.com

Counting numbers of "axioms" depends on which framework a theory is specified in, and also the formulation of the theory (which can be "golfed") . I find it somewhat entertaining but I wouldn't think too much into it.

The 271 axioms for Lean could be reduced by a lot if we specify it in second-order algebraic signatures. E.g. Martin-Löf type theory with reasonable features can be written in 28 rules there.
